data.title: Update underlying system expectations when adding a data mapping
data.when: A new feature or mapping is implemented that introduces complex state changes or modifies how existing structured data relates, but only the code logic has been updated thus far.
procedure: Review the source of the new mapped data structure (the 'amend' payload, in this case).
Identify all areas where the system relies on implicit assumptions about the data state or schema that are now violated by this new mapping.
Explicitly update the relevant expectation definitions, models, or service schemas to account for the full scope of the mapped data.
Verify that these expectation changes do not introduce unintended side effects into existing, stable functionality.
pitfalls: Only testing the new mapping feature's happy path while ignoring how the change affects upstream or downstream services (the 'silent schema drift').
Assuming that simply adding code logic is enough; failing to update the underlying configuration or model definitions.
Mistaking a temporary implementation detail for a permanent system expectation.
verification: Run full regression tests across both existing, untouched functionality and the new mapping path.
Manually review schema validation rules to ensure they explicitly handle the structure added by the mapping.
Confirm that the updated expectations are logged or visible in a centralized schema definition repository.
